# RTX 5080 four-target audit

User authorized the complete rerun on 2026-11-06, including repairs of
hardware/context failures and investigation of unexpectedly slow implementations.
This is sustained work, not a quick screen or a promise to ship sixteen flags.
Canonical source is `/home/philip/ShaderLOD` on Asahi; Windows gets a verified
runtime copy. Source, tests, definitions and compact findings are committed here;
raw captures, worlds, downloads and host-private paths stay outside Git.

## Decision and coverage

Determine which of G01–G10, C01–C02 and N01–N04 actually remove useful work on
the RTX 5080, across Complementary Reimagined and Unbound, BSL and MakeUp Ultra
Fast. Both Complementary profiles are tested, as one shader family. Reuse exact
original archives/full native settings from the Asahi audit, including separate
native-PBR parallax cases and no-op/fallback cases. Preserve native AA and the
actual Windows monitor mode: preflight observes 3840×2160, not Asahi's 2560×1600.
Cross-machine absolute times therefore have different viewport scope.

Use native Windows hardware OpenGL in the logged-in interactive console session.
WSL GPU/CUDA visibility does not establish this. Observe real GL version, renderer,
extensions and entry points. Exercise Minecraft's native context and explicitly
requested modern contexts where required (notably GL4.5 DSA for C02 and GL4.3
diagnostics); record the actual returned version. Never spoof capability strings.
Use matched baselines/controls for each materially different measured context;
do not mix contexts or treat a request as proof of the returned version.

## Procedure

1. Verify allocation, desktop/session, free storage, toolchain and canonical
   client inputs. Reuse prepared inputs/caches and `run_storage.copytree` checks.
2. Audit all64 cells and relevant historical failures. Use maintained `plan` and
   `check` commands for actual source, ownership, producer/consumer and work
   evidence. Repair viable generic source/runtime/GL contract mistakes. Missing
   native work, unsupported hardware and unsafe lifetime proof are distinct from
   repairable admission failures; no guard is removed solely to fill a cell.
3. Diagnose unexpectedly slow active routes, including instrumentation cost,
   extra programs/copies, native-equivalent compiler output, redundant admission
   checks and fallback work. Keep diagnostic acquisition outside scored windows.
   Measure repaired variants afresh. Do not infer that a slower mean is a bug,
   or that successful Apply proves useful execution.
4. Acquire two independent native-only baseline processes per target in the
   primary actual context. Use matched identical-pack null controls, including
   relevant scene/profile variants. Run at least two independent comparisons for
   executable cells, balancing ABBA/BAAB where the maintained route supports it;
   otherwise retain separate native/candidate/native brackets and matched
   native-equivalent controls. Extend repeats when noise, disagreement or useful
   apparent effects warrant it. No precision/benefit claim from independent-frame
   assumptions or a single discovery result.
5. Exercise varied relevant scenes, PBR where native work requires it, cases with
   little/no opportunity, and moving-camera quality for plausible survivors.
   Check shimmer, ghosting, disocclusion and transitions with honestly bounded
   acceptance. Preserve resolution/AA, errors and all restoration checks.
6. Export original baselines and every optimization with frame-time SD/variance
   within windows, window-mean variation and between-process variance when n>1.
   Keep scenes, context versions, implementations, phases and proven/fallback
   work cohorts separate. Publish interactive and standalone charts for all64
   cells, with explicit reasons instead of invented bars for unmeasured cells.
7. Verify all owned operations restored/released, retain evidence and useful
   caches, remove owned scratch, commit coherent checkpoints and push the branch.

The maintained `scripts/run_benchmark.py` owns timing, conditioning, controls,
admission, recovery and storage. No competing acquisition wrapper is introduced.
No user time limit was set. A checkpoint, failed check, low disk space or first
negative timing is not completion. Independent authorized preparation continues
while a required external input is pending.

## Initial findings and pending input

The configured Tailscale SSH alias reaches DESKTOP-E78LJSI with verified host key
and private-key authentication. NVIDIA reports RTX5080/driver617.42,0% utilization.
The previous GPU owner reports released work. Native Windows console session1
is active and its display is3840×2160. No Minecraft client was observed.

The user subsequently authorized cleanup of old ShaderLOD junk. The completed
[cleanup](CLEANUP.md) recovered3.735GiB physically after verified off-machine
preservation; about4.925GiB is now free, still below the32GiB reserve. The user explicitly declined expanding cleanup beyond ShaderLOD. NVIDIA caches
and other-project checkpoints remain untouched. The known retained ShaderLOD
Prism trees total only2.677GiB logically and contain useful recovery/world/runtime
inputs; removing all of them would still fall far short of the reserve. No native
profile copy or scored acquisition has started. Additional backing-volume capacity
remains required; this is not a negative optimization result.

## Capacity resolved and native setup resumed

A later native check observes63.2GiB free on C:. This is enough to start; the
80–100GiB suggestion was an initial allowance for build/cache growth and retained
4K captures, not a fixed admission minimum. The maintained32GiB reserve stays in
force. Capacity-checked canonical profiles and managed native/PBR slots now exist;
original archive identities match and the isolated native toolchain is prepared.
Initial dependency/build setup is in progress. Keep compact timing records and
preserve completed large captures off-machine as needed, instead of requiring all
campaign captures to accumulate on C:. No scope expansion to other-project cleanup.


## Native serialized acquisition

The Session1 launcher can serialize maintained commands using the existing
campaign queue helper. The versioned
[original/context queue](../../../benchmarks/campaigns/rtx5080-baselines-v1.json)
contains the remaining independent native baselines, separate optimized-stack and
GL4.6 BSL baselines, and actual4.3/4.5 startup checks. It contains no alternative
measurement code. The interactive launcher checks fresh owned outputs and exact
maintained CLI commands; the queue stops on failed restoration or remaining
clients. Its optional manual task time limit must cover the full serialized list.
Each operation retains the harness's own fixed timing, budget, storage and recovery
checks. The full source tree stays frozen on Windows while the queue is active.

# Source and correctness checks before 5080 acquisition

These are preparation findings and hypotheses, not RTX5080 timing results.
Storage now permits native setup and startup validation; no optimization timing
has yet been acquired.

The canonical source tree has a new maintained `--gl-context` option. Decompiled
NeoForge1.21.1 `Window` requests GL3.2 and can reuse an early-created window.
The explicit context path changes only the major/minor GLFW hints and disables
that early-window reuse through backed-up profile preparation. Actual returned
version must meet the minimum; no capability strings are overridden. Native
selection remains unchanged, frozen qualification refuses overrides, and the
sampler bootstrap admits only enumerated requests with the maintained controller.

Local validation:93 benchmark Python tests (2 platform skips),55 launcher tests,
the Java context-policy and sampler-admission tests, and development compilation
pass. This is not a live Windows context proof; the first native startup/check
must verify the mixin, early-window behavior and actual GL version before timing.

## Required mechanism evidence and regression investigations

| Goal | Required observation / specific issue to investigate |
| --- | --- |
| G01 | Actual copy calls and physical source/destination bank lifetime, not only a selected option. Revisit Complementary identity-pass proof with actual native graphs; do not reuse stale Asahi physical identities. BSL's live water reader cannot be removed solely to fill a cell. |
| G02 | Actual omitted mip/pass work, all live later consumers and fallback overhead. Compare source-only/native-equivalent variants when broad adapter overhead could mask a small saving. |
| G03 | Actual linked CUTOUT submissions and qualifying draw progress. Resolve platform/API and optional-stack refusals with source evidence; a flag or post-sample source declaration is insufficient. |
| G04 | Verify a contributing translucent-material case, source-controlled fast path, and separate water/no-op cases. Honey discovery did not reproduce on Asahi. |
| G05 | Distinguish shader-side projected refinement from MakeUp/BSL nearest-water permission. Exact-window grants are transient, so setup-time zero alone is not inactivity. Diagnose actual query eligibility and guard/driver cost before attributing a slowdown. |
| G06 | Actual qualified half-AO producer/consumer progress on Complementary/BSL; exact attenuation/center reuse is a separate MakeUp implementation. Half-AO source retains native near/HUD/sky and low-confidence fallback; coverage may be too low to repay the extra producer. The source is not an unconditional native-plus-half mix: full native work is conditional. This is a hypothesis to measure, not an isolated cause. |
| G07 | Typed actual depth/sampler ownership and permission progress in the timed window. Driver/GLSL equivalence and per-draw guard overhead may matter; a LOD0 expression is not proof of fewer physical transactions. |
| G08 | Native cloud/lighting eligibility and retained shadow/atlas semantics. Keep shader LOD reuse distinct from the private native-bound variant; small Asahi differences were drift-confounded. |
| G09 | Native POM must actually compile and use real height variation. Keep RP_MODE1 no-POM fallback separate from RP_MODE3/PBR. Diagnose cache codegen and prefix coverage; a source cache whose controlling uniform is optimized away is not proof of executed reuse. |
| G10 | Count exact duplicate-coordinate opportunities and preserve native arithmetic/filtering. Include native-equivalent private controls; tiny source-query opportunities and discovery-only gains do not establish hardware savings. |
| C01 | Real residual occluded geometry, query mode, command/primitive suppression and query/driver overhead. Preserve ordering and per-frame ownership; zero CPU reads are expected for the GPU conditional path. |
| C02 | Observe actual native NV extensions/entry points in GL4.5+ where required. Exercise existing 2×2 bloom tradeoff and draw/restoration witness; determine applicability to other target bloom graphs without pretending that an unsupported backend or absent extension is zero gain. |
| N01 | Real consuming compaction/cache hits and source/DrawID safety, plus CPU/driver time and actual workload bottleneck. Removed command-list entries are not removed GL draws. Use natural terrain rather than only the authored gallery. |
| N02 | Prove an attachment/target has no live/history consumers. Consolidate shared MakeUp deletion work with G01, without additive credit. |
| N03 | Prove terminal-copy liveness including next-frame/history use. Consolidate overlapping G01/N02 work and keep independently executable mechanisms separate. |
| N04 | Observe the exact overwritten/zero-work domain, source control and native fallback. Distinguish possible input eligibility from executed guarded branches and saved queries. |

The Minecraft source calls `RenderSystem.limitDisplayFPS` only when its effective
limit is below260; this runner's260 setting selects the native unlimited branch.
Do not invent a260fps measurement ceiling or change this setting without checking
the actual effective limiter/focus/VSync state.

At native3840×2160 the existing lossless quality recorder remains below its
4096×2160 pixel limit, and three121-frame raw RGBA8 sequences occupy about11.22GiB
before small metadata overhead, below the12GiB quality report cap. Actual capacity
checks and zero-missed-slot rules still apply; this is no justification for
lowering the maintained reserve. A later native check observes63.2GiB free,
which permits setup and one such capture while retaining headroom.

## Input setup inventory

Native Windows has an active console and existing PrismLauncher Java/game caches
and old ShaderLOD runs. They are protected; existing personal profiles are not
edited or reset. The p-stack native Python is available but lacks `psutil`, so the
benchmark needs its own dependency environment once capacity is available.
Original packs, native sidecars, canonical authored/natural saves and optional
PBR resources will be transferred/reused by exact identity through maintained
storage admission, not copied into a live or unverified personal instance.

The seven full native/default and PBR option maps now live in the versioned
`benchmarks/profiles/v1` directory with original ZIP identities. Their bytes match
the retained historical inputs; old paths were not moved. Maintained plan-only
preflight accepts the versioned MakeUp profile and explicit4.6 request at4K,
without launching or creating an operation. It correctly reports a stale build
binding after source/resource changes; the maintained execution command owns
the rebuild. This local plan fixture does not substitute for Windows preflight.

The Iris sampler repair's cleanup was also inspected: it skips already-zero
sampler slots and uses a single multibind where available. A larger tracked-unit
bound is therefore not evidence that every slot issues a driver call per draw.
Its real cost still needs measurement; do not diagnose it from the loop bound.

## Native Windows setup validation

The Windows runtime now builds successfully with the isolated JDK21 and Gradle9.2.1
cache; both client run configurations and all3,888 game assets are prepared.
Capacity-checked transport/copy/checkout verified515 profile files, both canonical
world maps and all original archive hashes. C: retains about60.7GiB after initial
setup;80–100GiB was not required. No other-project cleanup was performed.

Native Python benchmark tests initially exposed test-fixture portability problems:
two G10 tests referenced ignored historical option files, the POSIX-only legacy
storage module imported fcntl on Windows, and permission tests assumed POSIX chmod
bits. Tests now use the versioned byte-identical MakeUp profile, explicitly skip
the unsupported legacy POSIX storage class, and test Windows' supported read-only
bit while preserving the POSIX checks. The maintained run_storage/lifecycle paths
are not bypassed. Both hosts now run93 benchmark tests successfully: Asahi skips2
platform tests; Windows skips11 legacy POSIX tests. No production activation or
performance guard was relaxed. Actual Windows startup/restoration remains the
next live check.
